title: Domino Game
one_line: Trace, topple magic dominoes and sing along: ABC, Hindi and Bangla letters, 65 rhymes, numbers, animals, India, road safety and more, Nursery to Class 7, with English, Hindi or Bangla voice.
how_to_play: Tap once to start, tap a class and choose Run or Fly, pick a subject and a picture, trace the dots with your finger or mouse, then tap to topple the dominoes and watch the real picture stand up. Tap ABC to hear a name spelled, Sing to sing a rhyme with the words lighting up, and the purple note for a tune. The red play button shows a real video. The ? button explains everything with moving pictures; Games has Find it!, Spell it, Cross the Road, Draw my own and stories.
description:
Domino Game is where the learning path starts: a free game that builds the basics for children from Nursery to Class 7 through play. It has 838 pictures in 15 subjects, and every picture has a real dotted outline to trace: A to Z and a to z, the Hindi alphabet (varnamala) and the Bangla alphabet (barnamala), numbers, shapes and maths, the India map with all 28 states and 8 union territories, monuments, animals, plants, food, good habits, helpers, vehicles, the world, science and social studies for Class 6 and 7, and road safety.

When the outline is traced, dominoes stand up on it. Tap, and the falling dominoes play their own tune, then the real picture appears with its name. Tap ABC to hear it spelled, Sing for 65 rhymes in English, Hindi and Bengali, including poems by Tagore and Sukumar Ray, or tap the picture for an animal's own call.

Moving picture guides teach young children without reading. Real-life videos, Find it!, Spell it, Cross the Road, Draw my own, 14 stories, up to six players, stickers and a parents' report keep them coming back. Works offline once loaded, and nothing about the child leaves the device. Pictures: OpenMoji (CC BY-SA 4.0) and drawn for the game; maps: Natural Earth.
controls: Tap a class, then choose Run or Fly
Trace the dots with a finger or the mouse
ABC spells the name, Sing sings a rhyme, the note plays a tune, ? explains with moving pictures
tips: Let the child trace first; the helping hand shows the way if they get stuck.
Switch the voice to Hindi or Bangla to learn letters in the home language.
Open the parents' report to see what was learnt.
Play Cross the Road together before the walk to school.
story: I wanted young children to learn letters, rhymes and the world in the languages spoken at home, by touching and listening instead of reading. It is the first step of a learning path that continues in my other games, up to engineering and medicine.
